mike: Heads-up — nightly eval (2026-03-19 03:12Z) shows a sharp regression on the long-dialog prompt set when cache+batching are enabled. failure +12% vs baseline. :eyes:

sara: saw that on the dashboard. Is it correlated with the int8 quantized build we rolled yesterday?

olivia: i pulled the raw outputs — it's not deterministic: same seed + prompt sometimes returns an unrelated continuation. Happens more when batch_size >= 8.

dev-bot: CI job 7843 finished: nightly-eval/tokenstream_long_dialogs — 88/100 pass (baseline 100/100) — artifacts: https://ci.internal/nightly/7843/logs

mike: repro steps that hit it for me:
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"redwood-q-int8-2026-03","inputs":[{"id":"p1","text":"<long convo>"},{"id":"p2","text":"<different convo>"}],"batching":{"max_batch_size":16,"window_ms":20},"cache":true}' https://inference.internal/v1/batch
```

chris: i grabbed a few KV logs. snippet: `kv_slot=0x3a5f tenant_hash=0x7b2 collision_count=2 entries=[tenant:acme↔tenant:org-beta]` — looks like different prefixes map to same slot after our compacting hash post-quantize.

lena: interesting — could be that quantization changed tokenization boundaries slightly, shifting prefix bytes and increasing hash collisions under the new short-hash function.

sara: quick hypothesis: batching window merges requests so cache lookup uses combined prefix fingerprint; if two unrelated requests share a short fingerprint we serve stale continuation. explains nondeterminism and prompt-wise failures.

olivia: i ran a narrow repro: set `max_batch_size=1` OR `cache=false` and failure rate goes back to baseline. confirms interaction effect.

mike: mitigation ideas: 1) add per-tenant namespace salt to cache key (cheap) 2) increase hash width (more costly) 3) make cache key include request-id prefix + sequence-hash 4) tighten batching window to 5ms as a bandaid.

chris: can we do per-tenant salt in the serving layer today? we have tenant_id in header. should be low risk.

lena: agree — quick canary with salted cache namespace + small batch window change should show if collisions stop. i can prepare a canary image.

sara: mike — can you open an internal issue and assign the infra rollout? add links to CI logs and the KV snippet. i'll run the eval job after canary is up.

mike: opened GH #4829: "tokenstream merge collisions causing nondet gens" — assigned to lena/chris, linked CI artifacts.

dev-bot: deployment request: canary/redwood-q-int8-2026-03 -> env=canary (salted-cache=true, batching.window_ms=5) queued by lena

olivia: one more data point — the failures are concentrated on prompts that begin with long, repeated system prefixes (templates). that increases chance of identical short-hash fragments.

sara: action items:
- lena: roll canary with salted namespace + 5ms window (ETA 1h)
- chris: add KV collision counters and full 64-bit fingerprint logging for next 24h
- olivia: run nightly eval subset locally against canary once up
- mike: update GH #4829 with a short reproducible test and attach logs

mike: tagging @olivia @lena @chris — please update this thread when the canary finishes and when you have the eval numbers. :zap:

lena: starting rollout now, will post status.

chris: adding collision counter metric -> `cache.collisions.v2` and a tracing tag `kv.fp64` to the canary.

olivia: 👍 i'll kick off the quick eval once the canary reports healthy.

mike: thanks team — this aligns with expected batching+cache interaction risk. if canary looks good we'll plan a patch release and follow up on long-term hash widening. :thumbsup:
